- **Verdict**: the full text of Fuchs (2007) does not support "while within-moment experience remains intact". It places the disturbance in the retention–protention synthesis that, on Fuchs's Husserlian model, is part of each present moment ("consciousness is not momentary"), and it says single elements of experience become "alienated or opaque" and self-awareness is disturbed. What it does support is that patients stay conscious, and become more explicitly aware than usual. All three copies of the clause were reworded so that they keep only what the paper supports.
- **Source ledger**: Fuchs, T. (2007), "The Temporal Structure of Intentionality and Its Disturbance in Schizophrenia", *Psychopathology* 40(4), 229–235, doi 10.1159/000101365. Abstract from PubMed efetch 17396049. Full text from the author's copy at klinikum.uni-heidelberg.de/fileadmin/zpm/psychatrie/fuchs/Intentionality.pdf (7 pp., header "Psychopathology 2007;40:229–235", 4,437 words after pdftotext and whitespace collapse). Karger PDF returned 403; Unpaywall and Semantic Scholar list it as closed. Raw greps of the full text: "intact" 0, "preserved" 0, "spared" 0, "unimpair" 0, "unaffect" 0, "remain" 0; "within" 1 (p. 231, "lost within the sentence", which is unrelated); "self-awareness" 2; positive control "intentional arc" 19. Verbatim, each count 1:
  - p. 229 (abstract): "disturbances of self-awareness" among the basic symptoms "caused by a weakening and dissolution of the intentional arc"; "A failure of the continuous intertwining of succeeding moments, and especially of the protentional function".
  - p. 230 (thesis): "leaving single elements of perception, action and thought processes unconnected. Instead of carrying the intentional arc, they come to explicit awareness as alienated or opaque phenomena."
  - p. 231: "Thus consciousness is not momentary but spreads out by its double-faced attention of retention and protention"; the arc carries "what could be called an ‘implicit self-awareness’".
  - p. 233: "Patients have to compensate for this by an awareness of each single movement" (this supports "patients remain conscious").
  - p. 234 (conclusion): "In schizophrenia the protentional function may be weakened in such a way that the constant intertwining of succeeding conscious moments fails"; "the normal transparency of consciousness turns into opacity".
  - p. 235, the passage closest to the Map's clause: "patients are able to live from one moment to the next without experiencing a disruption of time". It describes a compensatory strategy (minimising change), not intact within-moment experience.

In the hub's words: "the mechanism the view owes by its own standard is not yet built, the illusionist declines to grant what the Map takes as a datum, that experience is what we know most directly, and functional roles underdetermine experience. Past these the disagreement is a boundary between frameworks, not a refutation." Three riders belong to the grade. Against the regress objection, Frankish "is right that the bare regress proves nothing". The programme is still being developed, so the Map's verdict is "a verdict on a live programme, not a defeated one". And the target is stated as the illusionist states it: illusionism denies phenomenal consciousness "as traditionally conceived", experience bearing qualitative properties "whether physical or non-physical", "not consciousness in every functional or everyday sense". Only the first ground presses the illusionist on a standard he accepts. The second and third are the Map's own starting points; the hub offers the third "from a commitment it chooses rather than derives". They supply what the illusionist declines and no evidence against him (P-M1).
  > - **Does not claim**: that illusionism is incoherent, self-undermining or self-stultifying; that the regress, Tallis or Strawson settles the matter; that illusionism denies consciousness in every sense; that the denial is a symptom of cognitive closure; that the mechanism cannot be built. Nothing here loosens the rejection either: the Map holds it, and the entry concedes nothing to epiphenomenalism.
  > - **Depends on**: Tenet 1 ([[tenets#^dualism|Dualism]]) as the source of the datum and of the underdetermination ground, a chosen starting point; [[positions/methodology-and-calibration#^p-m1|P-M1]] (a tenet removes a defeater and never upgrades the evidence); [[positions/arguments-for-dualism#^p-d1|P-D1]] (the datum is the phenomenal-realist premise the argument catalogue shares, so the rejection is not premise-disjoint from it); [[positions/arguments-for-mental-causation#^p-mc1|P-MC1]] (which already records that the Map meets illusionism "at a framework boundary"). *Leaned on by*, without edits here: P-CS1, P-AC4, P-MS1, P-VS1, P-VS3 and P-VS4 each name illusionism's vindication as a retirement condition, and this entry states what the reply they rest on has earned.
  > - **Argued in**: [[concepts/illusionism]] (the hub this entry transcribes), [[concepts/functional-seeming]]
  > - **Would shift if**: the mechanism were built: in the hub's words, "a mechanism meeting Frankish's two-part explanandum where the represented and the representing coincide would remove its main in-framework objection, leaving only the boundary disagreement". The grade would move the other way if "each attempt to specify the mechanism turns out to need what it denies—shown case by case, which the bare regress does not do". As an accounting claim the entry also shifts whenever the hub's wording does, and must then be re-transcribed.
  > - **Updated 2026-11-18**: entry created ([[reviews/optimistic-2026-11-18-positions-register|optimistic review 2026-11-18]]). The hub settled this wording on 2026-11-17 and no entry recorded it. - **Output**: [[research/basic-argument-and-constitutive-luck-2026-10-25]]

Raw encyclopedia text: SEP Skepticism About Moral Responsibility §2.2–2.4, Free Will §3.1, Moral Luck and Moral Responsibility §2.2.2; IEP Moral Luck. Abstracts: Hartman 2018, Strawson 2000, O'Connor 2009, and chapters of Levy 2011, Kane 1996, Mele 1995/2006, Clarke 2003 and Pereboom 2001. Metadata only: Clarke 2005a, Istvan 2011, Kane 2000, Williams 1976/1981 and five others.
- **Verdict**: `recommended_action: article`. Target: `concepts/basic-argument-and-constitutive-luck` (367/370; 2 slots after the queued collapse-priority-problem; topics/ is the fallback).

- **Key findings**:
  - "Evaluation awareness" names a classification ability. Representation, verbalisation and behaviour are weakly coupled, and verbalisation can be trained up 2.4–2.9 times with the probed belief held stable.
  - Causal tests that edit the trace disagree: Schoen et al. find an effect on one o3 evaluation; Knecht et al. find near-null effects across eight open-weight models. Knecht et al.'s explanation, that the answer is committed before awareness is voiced, is the host's concurrency break point.
  - Human symmetry holds. McCambridge et al. 2014 conclude that participation effects exist but that their conditions, mechanisms and magnitudes are not securely known. The Map's DES, protocol-analysis and process-content pages already carry the demand-characteristics caution.
  - Coiner correction: McCambridge et al. date "Hawthorne effect" to a 1953 textbook (French), not Landsberger 1958. Orne introduced "demand characteristics" in 1959.

## 11:30 - research-voids
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: The retraction void. A mind can withdraw a belief and remember withdrawing it, yet cannot see where the withdrawn item is still doing inferential work. Readers who "had clearly recalled" a correction kept drawing inferences from the old information (Wilkes & Leatherbarrow 1988), and continued influence "occurs even if the retraction itself is well remembered" (Ecker et al. 2010). The philosophical frame is Harman's coherence theory, on which no ledger of reasons is kept (1984a/b; Godden 2012 dissents on rationality; Doyle 1992; Gärdenfors 1992; AGM 1985). The note covers four faces: individual (debriefing perseverance, Ross et al. 1975 and Anderson et al. 1980; continued influence, Johnson & Seifert 1994; the Chan et al. 2017 and Walter & Tukachinsky 2020 meta-analyses), formal (reason maintenance, Doyle 1979; the worst-case complexity of revision, Eiter & Gottlob via Gogic et al. 1998), machine (edited facts recalled while multi-hop consequences fail, Zhong et al. 2023 and Cohen et al. 2024) and community (retracted papers cited as valid, Budd et al. 1998, Hsiao & Schneider 2021, Schneider et al. 2020).
- **Category**: Mixed.
  - Principally Occluded at the readout (natural): the withdrawal is registered and the reliance is unmarked.
  - Unexplored as territory: it is measurable as the gap between recall of the correction and inference, and it is moved by process debriefing, causal alternatives and warnings.
  - Not Unexplorable: reason-maintenance architectures propagate retractions. The worst-case complexity residue for complete propagation is recorded and not claimed.
- **Output**: [[research/voids-retraction-void-2026-10-24]]. `recommended_action: article`, `target_slug: retraction-void` (slug free in obsidian/archive/hugo).

## 07:57 - research-voids
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: The template void. Every reader of minds starts from itself (egocentric anchoring and adjustment, Epley et al. 2004; false consensus that survives education and feedback, Krueger & Clement 1994). Where reader and read differ in architecture, the template misfits, and the misfit can be recorded as a property of the read mind, not as the reader's limit (an "exported void"). Faces: cross-cultural (Elfenbein & Ambady 2002 meta-analysis: in-group advantage, smaller with exposure, majority members poorer at reading minorities than the reverse; Matsumoto's comment and the reply), cross-neurotype (the double-empathy literature: Milton 2012; Edey et al. 2016; Sheppard et al. 2016; Crompton et al. 2020/2025) and cross-species/system (de Waal 1999 by paraphrase; Colombatto & Fleming 2024).
- **Category**: Mixed. Principally Unexplored: measurable from a third position, and exposure, incentives and disclosure all move it. The first-person readout is naturally Occluded: a misfit does not present as a limit. Not Unexplorable; the only unexplorable residue is the general other-minds asymmetry, owned by voids-between-minds.

## 14:44 - research-topic
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Visual indexes and demonstrative reference without consciousness
- **Output**: [[research/visual-indexes-and-demonstrative-reference-2026-10-22]]
- **Sources consulted**: 47 cited.
  - Read in full and grep-verified: Pylyshyn 2001 (Wayback copy of the RuCCS reprint; the live URL is 404), Pylyshyn 2007 *Scholarpedia*, Mole's SEP "Attention" (2026 revision), Williams 2013 UCL thesis (the only raw source for Campbell 2002's own sentences), and Begby's NDPR review of Burge 2010.
  - The rest are PubMed, Crossref and OpenAlex abstracts. The 2005–06 *Phil. Stud.* symposium on Campbell is metadata only (Springer bot wall).
- **Finding**:
  - Pylyshyn's claim is preconceptual, not unconscious. His 2001 paper never discusses consciousness, and on p. 149 he drops "preattentive".
  - The "without consciousness" evidence is object-level attention without awareness (Norman et al. 2013, 2015), blindsight (Kentridge et al. 1999), neglect and extinction (Driver & Vuilleumier 2001; Mattingley et al. 1997) and object-file/percept divergence (Mitroff et al. 2005).
  - Against it: object-file updating was contingent on awareness in one paradigm (Lamy et al. 2015), a result Schoeberl et al. 2018 qualify.
  - No study found tracks unseen MOT targets. Scope: PubMed titles plus two web searches.
  - Campbell's sea-of-faces case grants reliable sub-personal pointing, so the vision science pressures his knowledge-of-reference thesis without refuting it.
- **Corrections to leads**:
  - Clark 2004 is a layered pluralist, not a critic of indexes.
  - Raftopoulos & Müller 2006 ground reference in object files *within* perceptual awareness.
  - Burge rejects both a consciousness condition (per Begby) and attribution-free reference (2022).
  - The Campbell–Pylyshyn exchange exists: Campbell 2007, *Mind & Language*.
  - The p. 45 Campbell sentence has two conflicting transcriptions (Williams; SEP), so it goes on the do-not-quote list.
  - Campbell's blindsight argument is still unverified.
- **Verdict**: article, `topics/visual-indexes-and-demonstrative-reference` (topics 358/370). A fold into singular-thought-and-acquaintance (3,065; headroom 934) was rejected because the weighing needs about 2,000 words; a one-sentence pointer is recommended instead.

## 10:12 - research-topic
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Immediate emotions and the affect heuristic in choice
- **Output**: [[research/immediate-emotions-and-the-affect-heuristic-in-choice-2026-10-22]]
- **Sources consulted**: 40 cited.
  - Nine read in full text and grep-verified: Loewenstein et al. 2001 (OCR copy); Slovic et al. 2007; Pfister & Böhm 2008; Sokol-Hessner et al. 2009; Davis et al. 2009 (re-grepped); Many Labs 2; Garg et al. 2018; Jäger et al. 2020; the Schlösser 2009 dissertation.
  - The rest are Crossref/OpenAlex abstracts, plus three reused from today's affective-forecasting-gap fork (Schlösser 2013, Young 2019, Dorison 2019).
  - Not reached: Lerner et al. 2015 and Loewenstein & Lerner 2003 (abstract or opening text only).
- **Finding**:
  - Felt affect at choice is measured and predicts choice, but it is not manipulated, and it tracks value.
  - Incidental affect moves valuation (sadness → choice price, replicated, d ≈ 0.43) but not risk preference at scale (Dong et al. 2026, n = 7,000, preregistered, null). This is a partial hit, confined to the risk domain, on miswanting's own stated P-VS1 falsifier.
  - Rottenstreich & Hsee 2001 Study 1 reversed in Many Labs 2.
  - Lerner & Keltner 2001 replicated for risk judgement, not risk preference (Lu et al. 2026).
  - Integral and incidental affect are not interchangeable (Ferrer & Ellis 2021).
  - The affect heuristic's "affect" is "with or without consciousness". The literature fits P-VS1 without evidencing it. No band change.
- **Corrections to leads**:
  - Slovic 2002/2007 is one text (EJOR reprint of the *Heuristics and Biases* chapter).
  - The time-pressure study is Finucane's Study 1, though Slovic calls it the "second study".
  - The integral/incidental definitions are verified in Peters 2006 and Pham 2007, not Lerner 2015 (not reached).
- **Verdict**: article, `topics/immediate-emotions-and-the-affect-heuristic` (topics 357/370). A fold was infeasible: affective-forecasting-gap is at 3,789 (hard_warning), miswanting at 3,188, and value-in-selection has 2 words of headroom.

- **Key findings**:
  - **A scope–phenomenality trade-off** (the Map's synthesis). Russell's acquaintance is presentation but licenses almost no singular thought about external particulars. Every view that restores ordinary singular thought (Evans, Lewis, Bach, Recanati, Sawyer) makes acquaintance non-phenomenal.
  - **The phenomenal condition survives only for perceptual demonstratives**, through Campbell 2002 and Smithies 2011, both non-dualists. Even there it yields consciousness-dependence, not dualism.

  - **Interpretability evidence** on entity representations (Meng 2022; Ferrando 2025; Sakata 2025; Yona 2026, preprint) tells against Hattiangadi & Schoubye's no-files premise at the vehicle level only.

- **Key finding**: the fork is **historically occupied, not assembled, and not exclusive**:
  - Locke (*Essay* II.i.15 [raw]) states the cost accounting against Cartesian dualists in 1690: "whatever ideas the mind can receive and contemplate without the help of the body, it is reasonable to conclude it can retain without the help of the body too".
  - Descartes partitions the fork, with corporeal memory in the brain and intellectual memory in the soul (Joyce 1997 [raw, opening pages]).
  - Broad (1925 [raw], pp. 359–360) coins "mnemic persistents" for the dormant remainder: "we know nothing with certainty about the intrinsic nature of traces". He adds a fourth branch, a trace-carrier with "strong reason to doubt that it has the higher factors of mentality" (p. 651).
  - The sleep test case is the Locke–Leibniz "soul always thinks" dispute, which has the same structure as the 2018 persistent-activity vs activity-silent exchange (Constantinidis et al.; Lundqvist, Herman & Miller).
  - Loftus & Loftus 1980: whether forgetting is loss of storage or loss of access "may be impossible to resolve in an absolute sense".
- **Corpus finding**: the Map is split, not silent. [[consciousness-and-memory]] L88 and [[episodic-memory]] L126 take option 1 (brain storage). [[filter-theory]] L75 rejects option 2 on engram evidence. [[bergson-and-duration]] L90 presents option 2 as aligned with filter theory without that caveat.
- **Ranking for the 3 slots**: veto > dormancy > observer-selection. Serial-order should fold into fusion-void (+1005 headroom). Grammar, contingency, perceptual-history and prevalence should fold.
- **Verification**: 15 new citations, every DOI checked at Crossref (Constantinidis et al. 2018 full seven-author list confirmed). Raw texts were grep-verified: Locke (Gutenberg #10615), Broad (archive.org scan, page heads), Leibniz (Bennett's paraphrastic EMT version, flagged), and Joyce's opening pages. Eccles ch. That choice study is unreplicated; Anvari et al. 2021 replicated only the misprediction studies, with mixed results. The strongest designs run through memory: Kahneman et al. 1993 (22 of 32 chose a dominated trial) and Redelmeier et al. 2003 (RCT, n = 682, OR 1.41). Immune neglect has only between-sample cases (Gilbert & Ebert; Kermer et al.). None measured felt anticipation at the moment of choice, which is P-VS1's input. Every route found is mechanism-neutral, so no P-VS1 band change.
- **Recommendation**: a short `concepts/miswanting` page of 1,500–1,900 body words (concepts 348/360), plus a zero-word pointer swap on `affective-forecasting-gap` L82, which is 3,616/3,500. Apply the swap only after the page exists. No section on the forecasting page.

- **Key finding**: the veto stays first, and its weak joint is repaired by **bypass**. Every intentional-inhibition paradigm read has to turn the veto into something else before it can observe it: a delay (Filevich et al. 2013 [raw]: the field struggles "largely because of the absence of behavioural markers of inhibition"), a statistical dip with no per-trial record (Matsuhashi & Hallett 2008), a labelled omission (Schel et al. 2014 [raw]) or an external cue (Schultze-Kraft 2016). A new first-person limb: when no action follows, intention reports fall from 35.2% to 16.0% (Schultze-Kraft et al. 2020; n=16; figures summariser-graded ×2). So cancelling an impulse also erodes the subject's own evidence that the impulse existed.
- **Triage decision-changer resolved**: the Schultze-Kraft 2016 main text reports **no** felt point of no return. Its questionnaire covered strategy only, and the SI was not obtainable. Face 3 stands as *unmeasured*, and Matsuhashi 2008 and Parés-Pujolràs 2019 narrow it: preparation is partly felt online, while no felt signal of the *deadline* has been reported. Clinical limb: urge intensity does not predict tic-suppression ability (Ganos et al. 2012), and children suppress tics without reporting urges (Banaschewski et al. 2003).
- **Closed flag**: in the Schultze-Kraft body, "ballistic" names the hypothesis the paper argues *against* (De Jong et al. 1990; Logan & Cowan 1984), which confirms the 10-06 fixes. The paper's PMC ref. 24 attaches the 2014 DOI to Logan & Cowan 1984, so do not copy it.

- **Sources consulted**: 16 (9 arXiv full texts grep-verified; Home & Whitaker 1997, Joos 1984, Joos & Zeh 1985 and both Laskey 2018 papers at metadata/abstract level only)
- **Finding**: standard Zeno theory holds for mixed states and multi-dimensional projectors (confinement, not freezing) and is an unconditional, non-selective effect, so Stapp's "makes no difference at all" is right about the state. It operates only inside the quadratic window; once the environment resolves inside from outside the leak is a rate and repeated projection changes nothing (Kiefer & Joos), which is Georgiev's redundancy regime. Stapp's equation (4) omits the environment during the interval. Where a brain sits between regimes is uncomputed. Note's own two-state derivation: rate ratio 1 − (1 − e^−x)/x, x = γτ, checked numerically.
- **Laskey lead**: verified. *Journal of Cognitive Science* 19(2), 125–163 (2018), DOI 10.17791/jcs.2018.19.2.125; abstract has the brain generating the templates. Bears on the Process 1 page's private-communication credit.

## 08:27 - research-topic
- **Status**: Success
- **Topic**: Anticipatory feeling and time preference: is the felt currency hyperbolic?
- **Output**: [[research/anticipatory-feeling-and-time-preference-2026-10-05]]
- **Task**: harvested from `reviews/optimistic-2026-10-04-agency-and-akrasia-wing.md` (New Article Subject 1); target `topics/`, intended slug `anticipatory-feeling-and-time-preference`.
- **Sources consulted**: 17 cited. 8 read as raw artefacts (Loewenstein 1987 and 1996, Story et al. 2013, Berns et al. 2006, Harris 2012 in full; Ainslie 2017, Iigaya et al. 2016, Kim & Zauberman 2009 in part); 9 abstract-only. 6 web searches.
- **Headline finding**: the test the-divided-will sets ("independently shown to be hyperbolic") has never been run. No study fits functional forms to a felt anticipatory measure. The models assume exponential rise (Loewenstein 1987; Story 2013) or constant dread (Berns 2006), and Story et al. set the hyperbolic form aside in so many words, saying the dread-augmented function depends "little on the precise shape of the basic discounting function".
- **The test is also mis-specified**: reversal needs non-stationarity, and a proximity-weighted anticipation term supplies it with exponential components. Loewenstein derives "reverse time inconsistency"; Harris (Study 4, N = 193, hypothetical shocks) reports a dread-driven reversal as the modal pattern (76% of the 103 who took 40 V now over 36 V in a week reversed with 24 weeks interposed), with the classic hyperbolic-direction reversal at 6%.
- **Split verdict for the Map**: on aversive outcomes a felt currency derives expedited pain, which hyperbolic outcome valuation only accommodates. On appetitive outcomes savouring favours delay, so the akratic reversal must come from impatience or visceral craving (Loewenstein 1996; Hardisty & Weber 2020), with no measured curve. The favourable asymmetry attaches to a felt currency and gives nothing to a unitary selector; Iigaya et al. (2020) put anticipatory utility in vmPFC.
- **Quote verification**: every quotation marked verbatim was script-matched against the raw text (62 quoted strings checked; the unmatched ones are abstract quotations checked against API output, plus one Harris range that was cut back because the PDF text layer has an unreadable glyph before the lower bound). Loewenstein 1987 quotations are whitespace-normalised from an OCR layer and flagged as such.
- **Task-lead correction**: the "2004 reprint" doi 10.1515/9781400829118-029 is the 1996 OBHDP paper (65(3), 272–292, doi 10.1006/obhd.1996.0028) reprinted as ch. 26 of *Advances in Behavioral Economics*; the 1996 original was the one read.
- **Not reached**: Frederick et al. 2002 and Loewenstein et al. 2001 beyond abstracts (image-only scans); Hardisty & Weber full text; the philosophical time-bias literature; any cue-versus-delay experiment testing Loewenstein's 1996 contrast. All listed in the note's Gaps section.
- **Chain**: `task_chains.pending_articles` entry added (target_section topics). Suggested follow-up beyond the expand-topic: a one-sentence correction to the-divided-will §accommodation.

The composite rival must be assembled from OSR-about-physics (Ladyman & Ross) plus structuralism-about-qualia (Loorits 2014; Fink/Kob/Lyre 2021; Lyre 2022) — and **both phenomenal structuralists decline the ontic reading**: Lyre, verbatim, "One might be inclined to ask whether neurophenomenal structuralism is a version of structural realism.
